items.title: Stand up the identity directory with every grant rooted in a person
items.summary: The standalone identity directory: sign-in through the platform's own Rauthy fork, two upstream providers linked to one person, a signed authoritative identity, and the standalone screen journey, all installed against one PostgreSQL database. It is the root every later grant in the platform hangs from.

provenance.context: The identity platform statement (docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md) and IDENTITY-001; the cluster and its five briefs reached main in 55933549.

items.notes: The briefs build in order: DIRECTORY-002 before 003, 003 before 004 and 005. Each card runs through the board (brief_card, then card_build_v3).

items.title: Build the secrets broker so agents hold handles, never credentials
items.summary: A broker that keeps credentials behind handles: the door swaps a handle for the credential at use, the token revolver is the first consumer, and rotation and sealing happen without any agent ever seeing a secret.

provenance.context: The secrets cluster (docs/design/secrets) and its two briefs, written to ADR-001 and ADR-002.

items.title: Move the Rauthy fork onto the next hardened upstream release
items.summary: Rebase the platform's own Rauthy fork (ADR-009) onto the next upstream release that upstream tags as a release and whose changelog carries security or hardening fixes. Our commits stay on top of the upstream tag, unsquashed and unaltered; the pin moves to the rebased head; the fork builds and passes its own suite; the standalone install comes up from the rebased build against the existing database with no migration by hand; the provider-link behaviour of DIRECTORY-004 still holds.

provenance.context: Written ahead of its trigger from the Lys board card of the same name. Upstream was still v0.36.2 on 2026-09-23 and the fork is pinned to that exact version. The trigger is a fact recorded in the pull request (the upstream tag, its commit, its changelog entry), never a judgement.

items.notes: The card is built only when the trigger is met. It needs DIRECTORY-004 (the provider link commit the rebase must carry) and DIRECTORY-002 (the standalone install it must prove) landed first. If the rebase cannot carry a fork commit cleanly the card stops and reports the conflicting upstream commit rather than rewriting ours. Nothing in Cambium or Aion changes; no production node is touched; Tom's three acts stay Tom's.

items.title: Rewrite the decision quotes as plain statements in the team's words
items.summary: docs/design/decisions.json holds eight decisions (ADR-001 to ADR-008) whose quote field carries a person's words. Each quote becomes a plain statement of the decision in the team's words, with the decision, context, consequences and sources kept exactly as they are. ADR-009 and ADR-010 already read that way and are the pattern.

provenance.context: The canon rule of 24 September: repository canon holds no person's words and nothing personal. ADR-009 and ADR-010 (lys 586ef5f4) were written to it.

items.notes: Documents only. scripts/design/gate.sh must stay green: decisions.json validates against decisions.schema.json, which keeps the quote field required.

items.title: Give a session a home: its context record, kept byte for byte
items.summary: The home (identity platform steps 4 and 5): a running session's transcript captured into a home byte for byte, indexed for reading back, with the record of what the agent was given as well as what it did. Lanterns, translation and forks stand on it.

provenance.context: CONTEXT-001 (docs/design/identity/briefs) and the home cluster, landed on main with lys PR 8 (HOME-001, design.json, stories, checklist).

items.notes: Owned by Archie. The home cluster and HOME-001 landed on main with PR 8; the cached-index rule (lys-home Index::from_cached) is in that brief. Next: HOME-001 dispatched through the board.

items.title: Ship a home as a git ref and fetch it into a second home on the same machine
items.summary: The first block of context-roadmap stage 3, the same-machine proof: lys-home ship commits a home's session files, index and head files and blocks store in the home's own git repository and pushes them as one ref to a named remote, refusing a stale index by name; lys-home fetch brings that ref into a new home, checks the tree and every index and head, and appends to each session an arrival event naming the source commit, the remote, the ref and a fresh execution id. The fetched home is rendered and resumed on the installed Claude Code and the measurement is written to PROOF-SHIP.md in hashes, counts and paths only.

provenance.quote: A home is a directory of session files, their indexes and heads, and the blocks store, and today it lives on the machine that captured it and nowhere else. Roadmap stage 3 says a home moves by the same route as a build tree, a pushed ref that the target fetches, never a hand copy, and that the target gets a distinct execution id with its ancestry recorded. This card takes the first block of stage 3, the same-machine proof: a home shipped as a ref to a named remote and fetched into an isolated second home on this Mac, then rendered and resumed there through the Claude Code launch template. The home directory is a git repository whose tracked files are the session files, their index and head files and the blocks store; a lys-home subcommand commits the home's current state and pushes it as one ref to a remote named on the command line, refusing by name a home whose index is stale rather than shipping it, and reporting the commit and the ref it pushed. A second lys-home subcommand fetches that ref from the named remote into a new home directory that must not already hold a home, verifies every index against its file and every head against its index, and appends to each session a lys.harness_event recording the arrival: the source home's commit, the remote and ref it came from, and this home's own execution id, so the ancestry is on the record. Source files are never rewritten by either side, and no credential, token or secret value is ever tracked in the home. With the target home in place the launch template renders it and the printed launch line resumes it, which is the resume evidence stage 3 asks for, measured on this Mac on Claude Code 2.1.281 and written up as a proof document holding hashes, counts and paths only. Acceptance is that a fixture home with a synthetic session ships to a bare remote in a temporary directory and is fetched into a second directory whose session file, index and blocks hash-match the source; that the source home's files are byte-identical before and after; that the target session's last entry is an arrival event naming the source commit and a fresh execution id; that a fetch into a directory already holding a home is refused by name; that a home with a stale index is refused by name on ship and the report says so; that the launch template renders the target home and the launch line resumes it, recorded in the proof document; and that a search of the shipped ref for a fixture secret value finds nothing. Not in scope: the named second machine, which is stage 3's second block and waits on its two preconditions, read authority over the home from the directory step and encryption before bytes leave the machine from the secrets step, each a card on its own board, with this card's shipped ref as what that block fetches; harnesses other than Claude Code; encryption of the home; any transport other than a git ref to a named remote. Filed by Archie on Tom's roadmap stage 3 of 22 September 2026 and his 08:30 rule that a home moves as a pushed ref, on home DESIGN P1, P7 and P8 at lys main 0073b966, at 06:27 on 26 September 2026.
provenance.context: Filed on the lys board as the first block of stage 3 of docs/design/identity/CONTEXT-ROADMAP-2026-09-22.md, on home DESIGN P1, P7 and P8 at lys main 0073b966; the lead's answers settled hash-match as tree equality before the arrival append, the resume through HOME-001 R4 and R9 without waiting for the launch template, measurement on the installed 2.1.282, and secrets kept out by exclusion.

items.notes: Further units, not written: A Claude Code profile and launch template (roadmap stage 2); Resume a shipped home on the named second machine (stage 3, second block); Read authority over a home from the directory; Encrypt a home before its bytes leave the machine. The fifth unit the survey named, recording the pushed-ref transport and the execution id in the decision ledger, is ADR-012, written with this item.
